_comment: The week in the C Cubed. The scheduled job appends one object to weeks[] after each week finalizes: a lede, a write-up for each of the six games, and an 'around' notebook covering everything else that moved that week. articles[] holds longer pieces — the Tuesday recap column, midweek previews, odds and big-trade pieces, the Saturday odds column, draft reports — written by the routines in ROUTINES.md or by hand. Every article carries a plain-text teaser ending in its own #news/<slug> link. A routine appends its one article and carries every existing one through untouched. The site sorts both newest-first and computes risers and sliders itself from its own power rankings, so nothing here should ever quote a rank or a movement.

weeks[].lede: one paragraph on the week as a whole - the shape of it, what mattered, what it set up

around[].kind: one of: trade, waivers, riser, slider, streak, injury, race, note
around[].headline: short, factual

articles[].headline: the piece's title
articles[].standfirst: optional short detail line next to the byline

blocks[].p: {type:'p', text, lead?}  - a paragraph; lead:true gets the drop cap. <b> is allowed, nothing else
blocks[].bars: {type:'bars', title, sub, rows:[{label, sub, value, group}]}  - diverging bars about zero; group 1-3 picks the colour
blocks[].cards: {type:'cards', items:[{title, big, sub, lead?, rows:[{label, value}]}]}
blocks[].img: {type:'img', src, alt, width?, height?, caption?, href?, link?, narrow?}  - an image from img/ in this repo, with alt text; href/link add a link under it; narrow is an optional img/ crop shown on phones (560px and under). Tapping the image opens it full size

articles[].teaser: plain text, at most 600 characters, no HTML, exactly these 10 lines: '🚨 C CUBED | WEEK n' (or PRESEASON), blank, the headline in capitals, blank, three lines that each open with an emoji and carry a stat printed in the article, blank, 'Full story 👇', and the card link https://drewkim623-hash.github.io/ccubed/news/<slug>.html (built by node build-cards.mjs)
articles[].source: which routine wrote it: tuesday (recap + column), watch (midweek: preview, odds, waivers, big trade), saturday (odds column)
articles[].kind: optional: 'opinion' for a piece that argues; the index flags it as a column
articles[].aliases: optional: older slugs that still open this piece (#news/<old>, #article/<old>, ?a=<old>). A replaced article keeps its old slug here so shared links keep working

blocks.text: Week 5 was the highest-scoring week of C Cubed's first season — 1,664.72 points across six games, 49.18 more than week 4 — and it ended both unbeaten starts. AB x B (asierbelay) scored 152.36, the most anyone has scored in a loss this season, and still went down to yerra x ecj (saiky7) by 6.08. Uzzz uzz uzz (jjnhwg) beat Jug (Lee284) by 23.48. That leaves four teams at 4-1 — saiky7, asierbelay, jjnhwg and Lee284 — and nobody else better than 3-2.
Jug's chance to make the playoffs on the site's odds board after week 5, the lowest of the four 4-1 teams. No other team in the league is above 66.4 percent.
Both Unbeaten Teams Lost on the Same Sunday

asierbelay and Lee284 came into the week 4-0 and left it 4-1. asierbelay's loss was the harder one to take. Drake Maye's 39.46 was the best score by any starter in the league, Jaylen Warren added 36.8, and the lineup's 152.36 would have beaten three of the six winners on the slate. CeeDee Lamb and Roman Wilson combined for 2.9 points at receiver in a game decided by 6.08.
Four Teams Above 87 Percent, Then Nobody Above 67

The standings show four teams at 4-1 and two at 3-2. The odds board, read after the week was final, draws a sharper line. saiky7 is at 93.2 percent to make the playoffs, asierbelay at 90.0, jjnhwg at 88.2 and Lee284 at 87.9. The next team, Tshough (tonypng), is at 66.4, 21.5 points below the lowest of the four. andychoe03 & NathKim are at 47.3, and the other six teams are all at 40.3 or lower.

Six of twelve teams make the playoffs, and there are nine regular-season weeks left. Nobody is mathematically in or out, and the board says so: 8 and thick (bigmoneyjos), the only team without a win, is still at 2.1 percent. But the four teams at 4-1 are priced as near-certainties, and only one other team is better than a coin flip.

blocks.text: The Season's First Trade Decided a Game Right Away

The first trade of C Cubed's season went through before week 5. andychoe03 & NathKim sent Josh Allen, Saquon Barkley and Zay Flowers to S2? #jtw #imwallin, run by yojarshh and Jopesii, for Davante Adams, George Pickens and David Montgomery.

andychoe03 started all three players from the deal: Pickens scored 28, Adams 22.1 and Montgomery 1.1; Montgomery is now out with a groin injury. Jacoby Brissett, picked up as a free agent the same week, scored 26.28 at quarterback in Allen's place, and andychoe03 beat tonypng by 1.78, the closest game of the week.

yojarshh started two of the three. Allen scored 31.5, the best of any yojarshh starter, and Flowers 14.6; Barkley, listed out with a hamstring injury, sat on the bench and scored 0. yojarshh lost to Terrorists (edyun1) by 36.68 and falls to 1-4, with a 15.8 percent playoff chance. andychoe03 is 3-2, at 47.3.
One week settles nothing about a six-player trade. andychoe03 started every piece received and won by 1.78; yojarshh left one of the three on the bench and lost by 36.68.
The Week in Full

Six games produced 1,664.72 points, the most of any week this season, and five teams scored 150 or more, also a season high. Two games were decided by single digits and three by more than 35. They are below in order of how close they finished.
The Trade Haul Holds Off Tshough by 1.78

andychoe03 127.28, tonypng 125.50. Parker Washington led andychoe03 with 30.4, ahead of George Pickens's 28, Jacoby Brissett's 26.28 and Davante Adams's 22.1. Those four scored 106.78 of the 127.28; the other six starters managed 20.5 between them, and Tyler Higbee's 13.3 sat on the bench.

Joe Burrow's 24.6 led tonypng, with D'Andre Swift at 17.3, Ka'imi Fairbairn at 17 and the Denver defense at 15. Brian Robinson, added as a free agent this week, started and scored 1.6. The 1.78-point margin is the second-closest of the season, behind tonypng's own 0.94-point win over bigmoneyjos in week 4. Both teams are 3-2.
asierbelay Scores 152.36 and Loses

saiky7 158.44, asierbelay 152.36. The 310.8 combined points were the most in any game this week. saiky7 had no starter above Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 22.8, but eight of ten reached double figures and seven scored at least 18.7, kicker Spencer Shrader's 21 among them.
Maye and Warren gave asierbelay the two best individual scores in the game, and Garrett Wilson added 23.4. Nothing else in the lineup cleared 20, and the Rams defense managed 3. Both teams are 4-1.
Eight Uzzz uzz uzz Starters Reach Double Figures
jjnhwg 144.64, Lee284 121.16. Jared Goff scored 28.94, Tyler Warren 21.4 and Derrick Henry 21, and the Houston defense added 16. Alvin Kamara's 2.6 was the only jjnhwg starter under 8.6.

Kicker Jason Myers's 23 led Lee284, ahead of Trey McBride's 21.6 and Ja'Marr Chase's 19.7, while Trevor Lawrence scored 22.74 on the bench, 5.58 more than the starter, Brock Purdy. Lee284's bench held 39.34 points in all. Both teams are 4-1.

nikhil1123 167.66, drewkim 132.20. Isaiah Likely scored 32.4 at tight end for n² (nikhil1123) and Jayden Daniels 32.26 at quarterback, and Justin Jefferson, Jameson Williams and Braelon Allen each added between 18.6 and 18.8. It is the best score of the week and the third-best of the season. Ollie Gordon, whose $55 claim in week 3 is still the biggest bid of the season, started and scored 14.8.
Christian Watson's 32.3 and James Cook's 22.8 led Lucky Strike (drewkim), but Jalen Hurts managed 13 at quarterback and four starters finished under eight points. Both teams are 2-3.
Team Meta/Bloomberg Wins With Nobody at Quarterback

jiddyyyyyy 151.40, bigmoneyjos 115.64. Team Meta/Bloomberg (jiddyyyyyy) started nobody at quarterback: Sleeper shows the slot empty and scoring 0, while Kirk Cousins, claimed off waivers this week for $0, scored 13.72 on the bench. It did not matter. Jahmyr Gibbs scored 37.7, Bucky Irving 31.5 and Malik Nabers 29.1, 98.3 points from three starters, and the San Francisco defense added 20.
Mike Evans's 26.3 led bigmoneyjos, whose 115.64 was the lowest score of the week. bigmoneyjos is 0-5, the only team without a win; jiddyyyyyy is 2-3.
Terrorists Get Their First Win

articles.headline: Nobody wanted a quarterback, and Josh Jacobs paid for it
articles.dek: Six backs, six receivers, two tight ends at the turn — and a top-32 running back still sitting there at pick 101.

cover.caption: The first four off the board: Gibbs, Robinson, Chase, Nacua.

blocks.text: The first draft this league has ever held ran on Sunday evening and took seventy-nine minutes end to end — fifteen rounds, a hundred and eighty picks, not one traded slot, and an average of twenty-seven seconds between names. For eight picks it went exactly the way the market said it would. Then it stopped doing that, and it never really started again.
the average gap between picks. A hundred and eighty of them, start to finish, in an hour and twenty minutes.
Six backs, six receivers, nothing else

The first round split exactly down the middle and touched no other position — no quarterback, no tight end, no thought given to either. It was also the most obedient stretch of the night: none of the first eight picks moved more than two places off its pre-draft price. jiddyyyyyy opened with Jahmyr Gibbs from the one slot, yojarshh took Bijan Robinson behind him, and the receivers came in the order the board had them.

The turn is where it loosened. drewkim took James Cook at 9 and andychoe03 took Chase Brown at 10, both roughly three picks ahead of the board, and from the back of the round nikhil1123 got Justin Jefferson at 12 and De'Von Achane at 13 — the only manager to leave the first two rounds with a receiver and a back both priced inside the top thirteen.
Two tight ends, then twenty picks of silence

edyun1 broke the position at 21 with Brock Bowers, fourteen picks ahead of the market, and Lee284 followed immediately with Trey McBride, seven ahead of his. Both of them play in tech, and having taken the two best tight ends off the board they then watched twenty picks go by before anyone else touched the position — Tyler Warren, to jjnhwg, at 42.
Thirty-three picks of everybody waiting for somebody else

Josh Allen went to andychoe03 at 34, and he was the first quarterback drafted. The twelfth team to take one was yojarshh, at pick 122. That is a room in which nobody wanted to be first, and the market punished the position all the way down: four starters with real prices sat there until somebody finally took pity.
Josh Jacobs, pick 101
picks past his price. Jacobs came off the pre-draft board at 31.4 and sat until saiky7 took him at 101 — the longest fall of the night by eight picks.

Nothing complicated happened to him. Six backs went in the first round and six more in the second, the run emptied out, and by the time the room came back around to running back it had moved on to receivers. Jacobs is the fourth back on saiky7's roster and cost a seventh-round slot. If the market was right about him in August, that is the single best price anybody paid all night.
Who could not wait

Three of the five biggest reaches were tight ends, and they came in a ten-pick window: Sam LaPorta to asierbelay at 83, Jake Ferguson to tonypng at 89, Dalton Kincaid to saiky7 at 92, each of them thirty-four to fifty-seven picks ahead of his price. All three had watched Bowers and McBride vanish at the turn. That is what a two-man cliff does to a room — it does not make anybody wait, it makes everybody jump early and separately.
Who let the board come to them

blocks.title: Picks gained against the market
blocks.sub: How far a manager's players fell past their pre-draft price, less what he spent going early. Positive means the board came to him. Colour is his division.

blocks.text: It is worth being careful with that chart, because it does not rank the drafts. Lee284 tops it and did come out with one of the better rosters — Chase, McBride, and then Jakobi Meyers and Brock Purdy arriving thirty-six and fifty-five picks beneath their prices. But the best roster in the draft belongs to yojarshh, who sits near the middle of it. He did not hunt bargains. He took Bijan Robinson second overall and then George Pickens, Rashee Rice and Davante Adams roughly where the board said, and that was enough.
What the twelve rosters are worth

Priced against the same pre-draft board, best fifteen picks each so nobody is paid for owning extra roster slots, the drafted rosters run from yojarshh at 112.8 points a week down to drewkim at 103.1. That is the whole league inside 9.65 points a week — and the projection only carries a little over half of a draft-day edge forward into scoring, because historically that is about how much of it actually shows up.
points a week between the best drafted roster and the twelfth. By opening weekend the model expects roughly half of that gap to still be there.

Which is the honest summary of the night. Twelve managers drafted, one of them clearly drafted better than the rest, and the reward for it is a projection that has him winning about seven and a half games out of fourteen. Nobody solved this on Sunday.

The Odds and Power boards label a team by its name wherever its manager has set one, so seven of these twelve read differently there: 8 and thick is bigmoneyjos, Lucky Strike is drewkim, AB x B is asierbelay, S2? #jtw #imwallin is yojarshh, n² is nikhil1123, Eug is Lee284 and Team Meta/Bloomberg is jiddyyyyyy. This piece names the managers throughout, as the draft board does.

Pre-draft prices are the Fantasy Football Calculator 12-team full-PPR board — 8,234 mock drafts sampled 23–30 August 2026, frozen on draft day and never updated, because the board that matters is the one that existed while people were picking. Twelve team defences and one tight end were not on it and are valued at the board's floor. Roster value counts each manager's best fifteen picks, one per round, so every team is priced on the same number of players. The projection those values feed is calibrated on a borrowed sample; the Odds board sets out exactly which, and why.

articles.headline: Three divisions, six places, and almost nothing between them
articles.dek: chaps drafted the best of it. tech drafted the closest. cville drafted the worst — and still owns a top-three seed.
articles.standfirst: Before a game has been played

cover.caption: One from each division, and the tight end who broke the turn.

blocks.text: Twelve teams, three divisions of four, fourteen weeks and six playoff places. The three division winners take the first three seeds whatever their records look like, and the two best of those get the bye. Everything below is a projection off the draft and nothing else — nobody has played a game — but the shape of the season is already fixed, and the shape says the divisions matter more than the rosters do.
of every team's games are inside its own division. You play each of your three rivals twice and everybody else once — checked against the schedule Sleeper has actually posted, not assumed.
The best of the draft, and the widest gap in it

yojarshh came out of the draft with the most valuable roster in the league — Bijan Robinson, Pickens, Rice, Adams — and he is the shortest price on the board to win the whole thing at +700. Behind him saiky7 holds the Josh Jacobs steal and a Jaxon Smith-Njigba–Drake London receiving pair, nikhil1123 has Jefferson and Achane from the back of round one, and jjnhwg has Jonathan Taylor and Derrick Henry and the least help behind them. As a group it drafted better than either of the others; it is also the division where the favourite is furthest clear of the field.
Three teams inside a point and a half

Lee284, jiddyyyyyy and edyun1 came out of the draft separated by 1.5 points a week — which, over fourteen games against a weekly swing of twenty-four points, is not a separation at all. The board prices them +230, +260 and +270 to win the division — forty points covering three teams, where no other division gets its top three inside a hundred — and the only reason it is a market at all is tonypng at +390. Two of these three teams also own the best tight ends in the league, taken back to back at 21 and 22, which is either the reason they are level or a coincidence that will look like a reason by November.
The worst division, and the cheapest bye in the league

On drafted value cville is the weakest of the three — 106.1 a week on average against chaps' 108.9 — and it holds the longest title price on the board in drewkim at +1500, with asierbelay at +1330 not far above him. bigmoneyjos is the favourite at +210 on the back of McCaffrey, A.J. Brown and Nico Collins, with andychoe03 and the only Josh Allen in the league behind him.

None of which stops one of these four from being seeded first or second in January. That is the format working as designed: win the softest division and you are a top-three seed regardless of what the other eight teams did. It shows up in the numbers as a wash — cville's four teams share 61.9% of a bye between them against chaps' 70.5%, a gap far smaller than the gap between the rosters.
Every roster against the league average

blocks.title: Drafted value, points a week
blocks.sub: Each roster measured against the average of all twelve, priced off the pre-draft market. Colour is division.

blocks.text: Nobody is a lock and nobody is out of it

Six of twelve teams make the playoffs, so the average team is a coin flip by definition. What is striking is how little the draft moved anyone off that coin flip: the best team in the league is projected to make it 60.4% of the time and the worst 41.4%, and every other team sits between them.

separate the best playoff odds in the league from the worst. Across fourteen games, that is the difference between 7.5 projected wins and 6.6 — the best draft in the league bought about nine-tenths of a win.

The win totals say the same thing in plainer language. Six teams are priced at seven and a half wins and six at six and a half, and not one projects above 7.5. There is no team here that has to be beaten and no team here that can be written off, which is the most anyone can honestly say about a league that has never played a down.

The Odds and Power boards label a team by its name wherever its manager has set one, so seven of these twelve read differently there: 8 and thick is bigmoneyjos, Lucky Strike is drewkim, AB x B is asierbelay, S2? #jtw #imwallin is yojarshh, n² is nikhil1123, Eug is Lee284 and Team Meta/Bloomberg is jiddyyyyyy. This piece names the managers throughout, as the draft board does.

Every number here comes off the same model the Odds and Power boards use — the same twenty thousand simulated seasons on the same fixed seed, so the figures in this piece and the prices on those boards are the same figures. Rosters are priced against the frozen pre-draft market; the calibration underneath is borrowed from another league's history because C Cubed has none of its own yet, and the Odds board explains what was borrowed and what it is worth. It gets refitted on C Cubed's own football the moment there is some.
